messages:
maya: heads-up - seeing a synchronized spike in attach latency across a small cohort in eu-central-3. GPUs stuck in PROVISIONING_WAIT.
oz: any storage signals?
ops-bot: [ALERT] eu-c3-cohort-5 nvme_gc_pause 0.4s -> 2.6s, write_latency p99=1.9s, media_errors +2 in 20m.
maya: dmesg on host eu-c3-56: `nvme0: sudden gc cycle, controller queued 1200 io` and a bunch of `I/O timeout` lines. Looks like firmware GC + janitor deep-scrub overlap.
oz: timeline shows janitor started deep-scrub at 1772468000 with concurrency=10, and a provisioning wave hit at 1772468045. Bad combo.
sre-lead: immediate mitigations: 1) pause deep-scrub for cohort-5, 2) set janitor concurrency to 2 for this cohort, 3) label nodes to block new onboards.
maya: applying now: `kubectl -n infra patch configmap janitor --type merge -p '{"data":{"cohort_overrides":"eu-c3-cohort-5:2"}}'` and `kubectl label nodes -l cohort=eu-c3-cohort-5 no-new-onboard=true`.
ops-bot: [INFO] patch applied by maya at 1772468120.
oz: can we avoid a big cross-region fallback? Cost-team: what's the impact if we shift 10% to eu-west2 for 1h?
cost-team: rough estimate ~$300 extra. Recommend limiting to critical lanes only.
maya: attach success climbed from 82% -> 97% in 6m after throttle. Queue drained. Opened INFRA-5123 to track: SMART ingestion, firmware GC telemetry, and scheduling scrub blackout windows during peak onboarding.
sre-lead: long-term: 1) add guardrail so janitor avoids cohorts with recent controller GC events, 2) ingest NVMe controller GC metrics into TSDB, 3) auto-label nodes when media_errors>3 in 30m.
maya: monitoring pinned, will follow up once SMART long tests complete. :thumbsup:
